title: Post-Quantum Coverage Register
description: Open specification for a verifiable post-quantum coverage register. A conforming register enumerates every data flow of a product with an honest status, binds each covered mechanism to an executable production probe, and defines signing, downgrade, and disclosure semantics. Published by HEOSSI (Pte.) Ltd.; reference implementation: Bee (bee.heossi.com/trust).

claim.description: The exact headline claim this register scopes. Marketing language must not exceed this sentence.

predecessor_hash.description: Canonical hash of the previous published version; null only for the first version.

exploitation_exception.description: Policy for delaying public detail (never the downgrade itself) when publication would aid active exploitation.

legal_scope.description: Statement of the register's legal character: factual scope declaration, precedence over marketing, non-warranty language, and contract version-pinning rule.

chain_policy.description: Where the canonical hash chain and the signature chain each begin, and how pre-canonical drafting history is recorded.

canonicalization.description: Deterministic serialization defining the signing preimage (e.g., UTF-8 JSON, lexicographically sorted keys, compact separators, sha384).

key_custody.description: Custody model for the register signing key, including the offline root and the online signer's authority limits.

envelope.description: The detached signature envelope: filename convention, schema reference, and the rule that the signature lives outside the register file (a file cannot contain a signature over itself).

public_key_publication.description: Where the ML-DSA verification key is published and how it is pinned across independent surfaces so a third party can verify without trusting a single channel.

downgrade_diff_policy.description: Machine-checkable whitelist bounding the online-downgrade signer's authority. Verifiers diff an online-downgrade version against its hash-bound predecessor (via predecessor_hash) using the PREDECESSOR's policy; any change outside this whitelist invalidates the envelope's authority. meta.signing must never appear in allowed_meta_fields, which makes the policy itself immutable under downgrade authority. This field exists because authority limits stated only in prose are not verifiable — the limit is spec data, enforced by tooling.

allowed_row_fields.description: Row fields an online-downgrade version may change; status changes are additionally constrained by allowed_status_transitions.

allowed_meta_fields.description: Meta fields that may change (typically version, date, predecessor_hash). Must not include signing.

changelog_rule.description: Existing changelog entries are immutable (prefix check); appended entries must carry probe_initiated: true.

transport_enforcement.description: prefer: hybrid offered and preferred, classical fallback permitted and measured. require: classical-only handshakes rejected.

release_signing_root.description: Long-horizon signing root. LMS (SP 800-208) on NSS-adjacent profiles, consistent with CNSA 2.0's exclusion of SLH-DSA.

ships.description: live = resolvable now; otherwise the phase at which the evidence surface ships.

qualifiers.description: Honest constraints on the status (e.g., client-negotiation dependency). Qualifiers are rendered with the row, never footnoted away.

closure.description: For excluded rows: the phase that closes the exclusion, or 'permanent' for boundary statements.

boundary_statement.description: True when the exclusion defines the platform boundary rather than a missing mechanism.

scope.description: mechanism: verifies a row's protecting mechanism; rows must reference it back (bidirectional binding). meta: verifies register infrastructure itself (e.g., evidence-link health) across rows without per-row binding.

published.description: Conforming registers publish probe implementations so third parties can execute the identical checks. Required true for covered-row probes.

detection_note.description: Honest statement of detection strength (e.g., sampling probability vs. exhaustive proof).

downgrade_trigger.description: Confirmed-failure rule that auto-downgrades a row (e.g., two consecutive fails; one fail for the end-to-end provenance probe).

inconclusive_handling.description: inconclusive (probe could not measure: probe error, network fault, dependency outage) pages the operator and never downgrades a row. Only confirmed mechanism failure downgrades. This distinction prevents probe-infrastructure faults or deliberate probe DoS from forcing public downgrades.

restoration.description: Return to covered requires the probe passing again AND a signed register change.
